ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, screen all shareholders, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners, banks, agents, and material counterparties against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union sanctions lists, Spanish domestic sanctions and terrorism-financing measures, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, and reputable commercial sanctions databases. Apply Spanish and EU PEP, family-member, and known-close-associate standards. Obtain source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, complex ownership, nominee arrangements, cash-intensive activity, unusual payment routes, or unexplained third-party payments. Escalate potential matches for documented resolution and prohibit onboarding until cleared. File suspicious-transaction reports with SEPBLAC where legally required; do not disclose such filing to the customer.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central online services operated through the Colegio de Registradores de la Propiedad, Mercantiles y de Bienes Muebles de España: https://www.rmc.es and https://sede.registradores.org
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be distinct from existing registered names and must include the legal-form designation or accepted abbreviation, such as Sociedad Limitada, Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada, S.L., or S.R.L. Names may generally be in Spanish or another language using permitted characters, but must not create confusion, unlawfully use protected names, or imply an activity or status not authorized by law. A Spanish name certificate is required before execution of the incorporation deed. Foreign transliterations and trademarks do not by themselves establish company-name availability or trademark clearance.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit an online name-clearance request to the Registro Mercantil Central with up to five proposed names in priority order. After issuance, use the certificate within three months for the incorporation deed; the certificate may generally be renewed once for an equivalent period if legally available, while the name reservation period is subject to the Commercial Registry Rules. If rejected, review the stated statutory reason, amend the proposed name, and submit a new application. A formal administrative or judicial challenge should be directed to the competent registry authority and, where applicable, the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith within the statutory deadline stated in the notice. The practical remedy is normally a corrected resubmission because name rejection is based on registrability and distinctiveness criteria.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Capital Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registered-office and correspondence purposes if it provides a genuine address, mail handling, corporate records access, and legally effective notices. It is not sufficient as the sole operational substance for high-precision injection molding, assembly, warehousing, inventory, product-safety compliance, or manufacturing activity. The company should maintain appropriate premises, equipment, supply-chain records, accounting records, and personnel or outsourced operational capacity proportionate to its activities.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No statutory probability is published. For a newly incorporated SL conducting ordinary low-risk manufacturing and trading without regulated products, cash activity, sanctions indicators, tax anomalies, or subsidy claims, the estimated likelihood of an unannounced physical inspection during the first 12 months is low, approximately below 5%. The estimate is non-binding and may increase materially for VAT-risk indicators, customs irregularities, worker-safety issues, consumer-product complaints, environmental matters, or inconsistent registered-office and operational information.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, Texto Refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC): Articles 9 (registered office), 20-24 (formation and deed of incorporation), 25-26 (inscription in the Mercantile Registry), 58-62 (share capital and certified payment), 175-197 (general meeting), 209-232 (administrators); Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre (SL de Formación Sucesiva regime).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (name reservation, Madrid) and Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office (definitive inscription); notarization before a Spanish Notario.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura de Constitución (public deed of incorporation) granted before a notary and inscribed in the Registro Mercantil Provincial; accompanying filings include Modelo 600 (AJD stamp-duty self-assessment) and Modelo 036 (AEAT census declaration for definitive NIF). Costs consist of regulated notarial and registry tariffs plus AJD (approx. EUR 30 for EUR 3,000 capital); there is no centralized state filing fee.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Standard SL: minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and fully paid in cash at incorporation; payment evidenced by a bank deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) or by a valuation expert report for in-kind contributions. Alternative: SL de Formación Sucesiva (SLFS) allows EUR 1 paid-up capital subject to statutory restrictions (mandatory allocation of 20% of annual profits to the legal reserve until capital and reserves reach EUR 3,000; prohibition of interim dividends; reduced member ceiling of 5). Non-resident founders may hold 100% of quotas and require a Spanish NIE.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously, by the founding members of [●], S.L., convened as the inaugural general meeting: First, to approve the draft articles of association and subscribe in full the initial share capital of EUR 3,000.00, fully paid in cash, evidenced by a bank deposit certificate under Article 62 of the Capital Companies Act, with shareholdings as set forth in the deed. Second, to adopt the registered office at [●], province of [●], and to ratify a corporate object comprising manufacture of toys and hobby goods under ISIC 3240. Third, to appoint [●] as Sole Administrator and [●] as Secretary, both accepting office, and to authorize the Sole Administrator to complete all notarial, registry, tax, and banking formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve Corporate Name (Certificado de Denominación Social)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), Madrid – telematic submission via the registradores.org portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for negative name certification (solicitud de certificación negativa de denominación) listing three to five proposed company names in descending order of preference. The RMC verifies that no identical or confusingly similar name exists. The resulting certificate is valid for a limited term (approximately 3-6 months, renewable), during which the incorporation deed must be executed.
required_dossiers: Completed certificate application form signed by all founders or an authorized representative
Copy of identification (DNI, passport or NIE) of each founder
Draft articles of association indicating the proposed corporate name
Proof of payment of the regulated name-reservation tariff (approx. EUR 10-15)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or already reserved, the RMC issues a reasoned denial; immediately refile using the next alternative name from the original priority list. If the certificate expires before the deed is executed, apply for a renewal or a new certificate without changing the registered name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Account and Deposit Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution (bank or savings bank) authorized by Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary corporate account in the name of the future SL (or in the joint names of the founders) and deposit the full EUR 3,000 capital. Instruct the bank to issue a statutory capital-deposit certificate in the intended corporate name, identifying each depositor and amount paid. The certificate must be delivered to the notary before execution of the deed and is later released once the definitive corporate account is opened after registration.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of each founding member
Approved name certificate or certified copy of the name reservation
Signed account-opening application and bank KYC/AML declaration
Proof of deposit (bank transfer or cash-in slip)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank identifies a mismatch between the account name and the certified name, obtain a corrected certificate before the notarial appointment. If the certificate lapses (typically after six months), replenish the deposit or request a revalidation letter from the bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Deed of Incorporation before Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario (Spanish notary public) of the district of the registered office or chosen by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear before the notary in person or by sufficient power of attorney. The notary verifies legal capacity, reads and checks the draft bylaws, records the name certificate and the bank capital-deposit certificate, and simultaneously requests a provisional tax identification number (NIF provisional) from AEAT by telematic channel. The deed must state the founders, corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, share capital and quota allocations, and the administration regime.
required_dossiers: Draft deed and articles of association (estatutos)
Original bank capital-deposit certificate
Original name certificate issued by the Registro Mercantil Central
Identity documents (DNI, passport or NIE) of all founders; NIE application for non-residents processed at the Spanish consulate or police station
Power of attorney with legalization or apostille, if a founder acts by representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections to any clause, amend the bylaws and execute a corrected deed before the same notary. If a founder is unavailable, obtain a duly authenticated notarial power of attorney and re-execute the deed; the provisional NIF request is regenerated automatically with the new deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Provisional NIF and Self-Assess Stamp Duty (AJD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) for NIF; regional tax authority (Consejería de Hacienda or delegated liquidating office) for Modelo 600
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the provisional NIF issued at the notary stage or apply via Modelo 036 at AEAT. Within 30 working days from execution of the deed, self-assess the Impuesto de Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados (AJD) on Modelo 600. The standard rate is 1% of capital (approx. EUR 30 for EUR 3,000), subject to reduced regional rates and to exemptions applicable to SLFS incorporations. Keep the stamped settlement receipt for submission to the Mercantile Registry.
required_dossiers: Modelo 600 (AJD self-assessment) duly completed
First copy (primera copia) of the notarial deed of incorporation
Provisional NIF certificate
Authorized second copy of the deed, if the first copy must be retained by the financing bank or notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Modelo 600 return is rejected or queried, correct and refile the return, paying any supplementary amount with the applicable late-payment surcharge if the statutory deadline is missed; obtain the stamped settlement statement (justificante) before proceeding to registry inscription.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscribe the Company in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the first copy of the notarial deed, the AJD settlement statement, and the provisional NIF certificate with the Mercantile Registry as soon as possible after execution. The registrar examines the legal validity of the deed under the Capital Companies Act and the Mercantile Registry Regulations; upon favorable qualification, the company acquires full legal personality with retroactive effect to the date of the deed, and the incorporation is published in the BORME (Boletín Oficial del Registro Mercantil).
required_dossiers: First copy of the notarial deed of incorporation
Certified copy or original of the AJD payment (Modelo 600)
Provisional NIF certificate
Bank capital-deposit certificate attached to the deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of defects (deficiencias) or suspension, file a corrective instrument (escritura de subsanación) within the granted term, usually two months. If registration is refused outright, appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within two months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Definitive NIF and Complete Tax Census Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT – local or delegated tax office in the jurisdiction of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the registry inscription, present Modelo 036 at AEAT to convert the provisional NIF into a definitive NIF. Complete the census declaration with the full corporate details, registered office address, and the ISIC 3240 activity code; register for the Impuesto de Actividades Económicas (IAE) insofar as required; and enroll for electronic filing. Also request the company digital certificate from the FNMT-CERES for future e-filing obligations.
required_dossiers: Modelo 036 (census declaration) completed and signed by the legal representative
Certificate of registration (certificado de inscripción) issued by the Mercantile Registry
Copy of the notarial deed and the provisional NIF certificate
Power of attorney for the filing agent, if applicable
Identity document (DNI or NIE) of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT detects inconsistencies in the census data, correct the declaration and resubmit Modelo 036; if the provisional NIF has lapsed before definitive conversion, reinitiate the procedure through the notary and AEAT with the supporting deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as Employer with Social Security and Prepare Pre-Operation Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS), provincial directorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer by applying for an employer identification code (código de cuenta de cotización) at the TGSS, either electronically through the Cert@red system or in person. Enroll the sole administrator in the RETA regime if the office is performed in a remunerated executive capacity. Obtain the company electronic signature certificate and, where required, finalize the Modelo 036 IAE registration at AEAT. This step is a mandatory precondition for hiring employees and issuing payroll obligations.
required_dossiers: Modelo TA.7 (employer registration) or the telematic RED/Cert@red application
Definitive NIF certificate and certified copy of the notarial deed
Identity document and NIE/DNI of the legal representative
Authorization form for the RED system and company digital certificate request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the TGSS rejects the application due to missing or incorrect data, rectify the Modelo TA.7 and resubmit; if the administrator’s inclusion in the RETA is disputed, file a rectification request with the TGSS or engage a social-security gestor to align the situation with the social-security administrative records.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Consejería de Industria / Dirección General de Industria, Energía y Minas of the relevant Autonomous Community (regional industrial authority) in coordination with the Ayuntamiento (municipal government) for activity and opening licensing; the central industrial database is the Registro Integrado Industrial (RII). Toy manufacture itself is not subject to prior sectoral authorization in Spain — market access requires CE marking under Real Decreto 1205/2011 — but physical operation of an industrial plant requires municipal activity licensing and the pre-commencement communication to the industrial registry.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Actividad y Apertura (or Declaración Responsable de Inicio de Actividad for low-risk activities under municipal ordinances implementing Directive 2006/123/CE and Ley 39/2015); plus Comunicación de Puesta en Marcha del Establecimiento Industrial (Ley 21/1992, de Industria, art. 14, as implemented by regional industry regulations); toy CE conformity under Real Decreto 1205/2011, de 26 de agosto (transposing Directive 2009/48/CE).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería de Medio Ambiente of the Autonomous Community (regional environmental authority); state coordination by the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) when cross-autonomous or transboundary environmental effects may arise.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Simplified EIA (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Simplificada) under Ley 21/2013, de 9 de diciembre, de evaluación ambiental, Annex II, for medium-sized industrial installations exceeding municipal thresholds. In practice, small injection-molding toy workshops are treated as classified activities (actividades clasificadas) subject only to a municipal environmental-activity license or environmental declaration, unless installed power, land area, or production capacity exceeds the Ley 21/2013 Annex I/II thresholds, which would require a full EIA study (Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental Ordinaria).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: discharge to municipal sewer only with a sewer-discharge permit under the local sanitation ordinance (typical limits: pH 6-9, TSS ≤500 mg/L, COD ≤1,000 mg/L); industrial process water must not be discharged without prior authorization under Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2001 (Ley de Aguas). Air and VOC: compliance with Real Decreto 117/2003 limits if annual solvent consumption equals or exceeds 150 tonnes; otherwise maintain odor, particulate, and fume emissions below local nuisance thresholds. Noise: compliance with Ley 37/2003 and Real Decreto 1367/2007, generally LAeq ≤60-65 dBA at the plant boundary in daytime industrial zoning. Waste: hazardous-waste segregation and traceability under Ley 7/2022, de residuos y suelos contaminados, and packaging-waste extended-producer-responsibility obligations under Real Decreto 1055/2022, de envases y residuos de envases.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certification of the industrial premises under Real Decreto 2267/2004 (Reglamento de seguridad contra incendios en los establecimientos industriales) with a technical project and municipal fire-department inspection; building structural-load certificate for injection-molding machines; occupational risk-prevention plan under Ley 31/1995 and workplace-conditions compliance under Real Decreto 486/1997 (workplaces), Real Decreto 1215/1997 (work equipment), Real Decreto 773/1997 (personal protective equipment), and Real Decreto 842/2002 (REBT electrical installations); appointment of a prevention service and registration of the risk-prevention plan, employee training records, and medical-surveillance protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); business census registry: Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores; commercial incorporation registry: Registro Mercantil Central.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) owned by non-residents: (1) each non-resident founder obtains an NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero) from the Spanish Consulate or local immigration office; (2) reserve the company name at the Registro Mercantil Central (certificación de denominación social); (3) file modelo 036 with AEAT to obtain a provisional NIF prior to notarisation; (4) execute the public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) before a Spanish notary, deposit it at the Registro Mercantil, and file modelo 600 (TIE/JP) for capital transfer tax formalities; (5) within 30 days of deed registration, submit modelo 036 to obtain the definitive NIF (for an SL: letter 'B' + 7 digits + control character); (6) register in the Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores and, if annual turnover exceeds EUR 1 million or intra-EU acquisitions exceed EUR 10,000, obtain a NIF-IVA (VAT identification number); (7) secure an electronic certificate (FNMT digital certificate) for mandatory electronic filing through the AEAT portal; (8) foreign entities without a permanent establishment must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) resident in Spain, registered via modelo 036.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Impuesto sobre Sociedades; general CIT rate 25%; reduced 15% for newly created SLs in the first two tax periods with positive taxable base). Territorial scope: worldwide taxation for tax-resident SLs; foreign partners are taxed under Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) only on Spanish-source income. Tax-Exempt Zone: Canary Islands ZEC (Zona Especial Canaria) offers 4% CIT and reduced VAT (IGIC) for approved manufacturing/trading entities established in the Canary Islands. No pass-through transparency for Spanish SLs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; elections embedded in Spanish law: (1) tax consolidation regime for groups with 75%+ ownership (Art. 64-79 LIS); (2) merger/reorganisation neutrality regime deferring built-in gains (Art. 76-89 LIS); (3) 15% reduced CIT for new SLs (Art. 29.3 LIS) tapering to 25% thereafter; (4) ETVE/participation-exemption election for qualifying foreign dividends and capital gains (Art. 21 LIS); (5) cash-basis VAT (criterio de caja) for SMEs with turnover up to EUR 2 million, deferred VAT payment until customer payment; (6) monthly VAT refund regime for regular exporters (election via modelo 036 enabling refunds in each monthly 303 return); (7) EU SME VAT exemption election (from 1 Jan 2025) for businesses with turnover up to EUR 85,000 domestic / EUR 100,000 intra-EU; (8) cross-border loss relief and foreign tax credit elections under the LIS anti-double-taxation framework (Art. 31-32 LIS).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 and Royal Decree 1624/1992, transposing EU Directive 2006/112/EC; special regimes: SME simplified regime, group VAT (régimen de grupo de entidades), travel agents, and distance-sales OSS/IOSS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general domestic monetary threshold: any person commencing taxable economic activity in Spanish territory must register in the Censo de Empresarios (modelo 036/037) before the first transaction, regardless of turnover. Optional SME exemption effective 1 Jan 2025: businesses with annual turnover in Spain below EUR 85,000 and intra-EU cross-border supplies below EUR 100,000 may elect full VAT exemption; otherwise registration is mandatory and VAT applies from the first sale.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Near-real-time fiscal clearance via SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información): mandatory for taxpayers with turnover > EUR 6,010,121.41 or in consolidated VAT groups; invoice records must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days (8 for certain records) of issue via web service/API. Verifactu (RD 1007/2023, applicable from 2025): all invoicing software must generate non-editable, hash-chained invoice records and display a QR Verifactu on each invoice, allowing AEAT real-time access to invoice integrity. Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) mandates structured B2B e-invoicing (Facturae 3.2 XML or equivalent UN/CEFACT CII/UBL) with the implementing royal decree expected to phase in application one year after publication for enterprises > EUR 8 million turnover and two years for SMEs; B2G invoicing through the FACe platform is already compulsory. Exports are cleared through the electronic customs declaration (e-DUA) in the AEAT customs system, not by fiscal stamping of invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of ISIC 3240 mecha model kits to non-EU buyers are exempt with refund (0% IVA) under Art. 21 LIVA provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch (AEAT may extend to 180 days on justified request) and the exporter retains accepted documentary proof of exit. Intra-EU zero-rated supplies under Art. 25 LIVA require the customer's valid EU VAT number recorded in the VIES database, dispatch of goods to another Member State, and filing of the recapitulative EC Sales List (modelo 349) plus Intrastat if the annual threshold is exceeded. Export-related services (international transport, loading, customs agency, design and offshore support services supplied to non-EU customers) are also zero-rated. The exporter must demonstrate that it holds the goods, is the declarant, and that the export invoice is issued in the name of the exporter; e-commerce export consignments may be zero-rated when dispatched with the parcel operator and covered by the exporter's DUA. Refunds of input VAT on export costs are claimed through the periodic modelo 303 return, or monthly under the devolución mensual election for regular exporters; non-established businesses use modelo 361 (Refund Directive) via the AEAT portal.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) lodged electronically and accepted by the Customs Office of departure, with the Export Accompanying Document (EAD) and indication of exit via the NCTS system

Proof of exit of the goods: Bill of Lading (maritime), Air Waybill (air), CMR road consignment note, or customs exit-stamped copy of the Single Administrative Document issued or validated by the Customs office of exit

Commercial invoice, packing list, P&L weight/unit price documentation, and bank payment certificate (inward remittance certificate/certificado de cobro) evidencing collection of export proceeds; for intra-EU supplies also the EC Sales List (modelo 349) and Intrastat declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT verifies export exemption substantiation under Art. 23-24, 26 and 30 LIVA. Missing, defective, or fraudulent export documentation re-characterises the sale as a domestic taxable transaction at 21% IVA, with late-payment interest from the original due date, surcharges of 20%-35% (período ejecutivo), and a penalty under Art. 170 and 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the tax evaded where culpability is established. Criminal fraud under Art. 305 Código Penal (1-6 years imprisonment) applies when the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period; the four-year limitation period for the right to assess tax (10 years for fraudulently concealed gains) enables retrospective clawbacks. Although Spain imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline, AEAT treats uncollected export receivables beyond 180 days from the DUA as a red flag requiring proof of collection; overdue balances may be reclassified as taxable income or deemed loans attracting imputation, and transactions with non-residents above EUR 50,000 must be reported to Banco de España in the Balance of Payments statistical declaration. The taxpayer bears the burden of proving the physical exit of goods and receipt of payment within the 90/180-day window.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates a fully convertible Euro regime. Capital account transactions are liberalized for EU counterparties with no prior approval required. Non-resident profit remittances are permitted after Spanish tax withholding and beneficial ownership verification. Hurdles include CRS/FATCA reporting obligations and potential CFC or anti-avoidance rules.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds to authorized dealers. Receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts or applied to current account transactions. All exports require customs declaration, VAT-compliant invoicing, and annual corporate tax filing with no statutory conversion timeline.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: PayPal Business and similar EMI platforms are available to Spanish SL entities but subject to volume limits and cross-border restrictions. Legal constraints include mandatory NIF registration, full AML/KYC due diligence, and PSD2 compliance. Offshore digital EMIs face heightened scrutiny for transaction monitoring and tax reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors, authorized signatories, and beneficial owners must appear physically for KYC interviews and document verification at bank branches. Remote corporate account opening is not permitted under Spanish regulations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association, shareholder registry extracts, and proof of ultimate beneficial owners
Export contracts, manufacturing invoices, audited financial statements, and bank references

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires use SWIFT MT103 with IBAN, purpose codes such as 'Payment for goods' or 'Share capital injection', and matching invoices. Verification requires beneficial owner attestation, tax ID confirmation, and AML source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements via SWIFT MT103 or commercial Letters of Credit. Trade disbursements require supporting documentation including purchase orders, shipping documents, bills of lading, and tax-compliant invoices.

stage_5.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Rules regarding annual confirmation for shareholding transfers
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory eligibility and anti-abuse conditions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Key incentives include a 15% rate for qualifying newly incorporated entities, research and development and technological innovation tax credits, deductions for certain investments, capitalization reserve and employment reserve regimes, and participation exemption treatment for qualifying dividends and capital gains. The applicable rate and eligibility must be confirmed against the entity's turnover, group status, activity, and tax period.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry. Tax losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, subject to utilization limits based principally on the taxpayer's net turnover and applicable anti-abuse rules. As a general rule, utilization is limited to 70% of positive taxable income before loss utilization, with a EUR 1,000,000 minimum annual offset; lower percentage limits apply to larger taxpayers.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where available, or an authorized representative. Modelo 202 is used for advance corporate income tax payments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 200: annual. Modelo 202: generally three advance-payment periods per year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is generally due within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; for non-calendar tax years, the periods are calculated by reference to the fourth, tenth, and thirteenth months after the start of the tax year. Electronic filing deadlines are subject to AEAT calendar rules and extensions where the final day is not a permitted filing day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period dates, legal form, activity classification, and representative details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish entity's own NIF. A non-resident shareholder does not replace the Spanish SL as the taxpayer. Report foreign parent information only where the form specifically requests ownership, group, related-party, or representative data.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss according to the approved statutory accounts before corporate income tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish SL must report its Spanish statutory-accounting result. Foreign parent accounting results are excluded unless attributable to the Spanish entity or required under a specific tax consolidation regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and deductions for non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, financial expense limitations, related-party adjustments, and other statutory differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude expenses incurred solely by a non-resident shareholder. Include only expenses economically attributable to the Spanish entity and supported by accounting records and commercial evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior periods used in the current period, together with remaining balances and applicable utilization limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses generated by another group company cannot be imported into the Spanish SL outside an authorized tax consolidation regime. Acquisition of a loss-making company may trigger anti-abuse restrictions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, double-taxation relief, employment-related deductions, and other legally available credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim cross-border relief only where the income, foreign tax, beneficial ownership, and documentary evidence satisfy Spanish domestic law and the applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax base and gross tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after adjustments and loss utilization, multiplied by the applicable corporate tax rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% general rate unless the entity demonstrably qualifies for a preferential rate. Do not apply a non-resident parent's tax rate to the Spanish SL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding tax suffered and Modelo 202 advance payments creditable against the final corporate income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign withholding tax is not automatically creditable. Apply Spanish foreign-tax-credit limitations, treaty rules, source-income matching, and supporting certificate requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, refund, or balance due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance after credits, with payment or refund instructions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made through approved AEAT payment channels. A refund requires a valid Spanish bank account or an accepted alternative procedure and may be subject to verification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related parties and, where applicable, submission of related-party transaction information and transfer-pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose dealings with foreign shareholders, group manufacturers, distributors, licensors, financiers, and service companies when they meet Spanish related-party rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indication of tax consolidation, restructuring, holding-company, merger, or other special regimes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent cannot itself be treated as a Spanish tax-consolidated entity unless statutory Spanish and European Economic Area requirements are satisfied and the relevant election and filings are completed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized electronic signature, submission receipt, payment reference, and supporting documentation retained for audit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Spanish legal representative or authorized tax agent must maintain authority evidence, corporate records, and electronic submission confirmations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file without economic damage generally attracts a fixed penalty under the General Tax Law, normally EUR 200, reduced by 50% for voluntary filing where applicable and potentially increased after an administrative requirement. Returns causing economic damage may attract a penalty generally calculated at 1% of the unpaid amount plus 1% for each full month of delay during the first 12 months, and 15% plus statutory late-payment interest after 12 months, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Late payment surcharges generally increase by 1% for each full month of delay up to 12 months, followed by a 15% surcharge plus interest. Understatement or concealment can generate penalties of 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, depending on severity.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident recipient, subject to domestic exemptions, European Union relief, treaty reductions, beneficial ownership, anti-abuse rules, and procedural compliance. A qualifying EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may eliminate withholding where the statutory ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify beneficial ownership, treaty eligibility, ownership percentage, holding period, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose considerations where relevant, and the recipient's legal form. Apply the reduced treaty rate or exemption only where the payer has sufficient documentation. If Spanish withholding is imposed, the recipient may generally seek a refund through AEAT procedures using proof of residence, payment evidence, withholding certificates, and beneficial-ownership documentation. Treaty relief is not available for conduit arrangements or arrangements lacking commercial substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The standard Spanish non-resident withholding rate is generally 24% for royalties, interest, and similar income paid to non-residents outside the EU or European Economic Area, while a 19% rate generally applies to qualifying EU or EEA recipients under domestic rules. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated companies satisfying ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse requirements. Tax treaties commonly reduce rates, frequently to 0% to 10% for interest and 5% to 10% for royalties, but the applicable treaty must be checked individually. Arm's-length pricing, beneficial ownership, withholding certificates, and anti-hybrid and anti-abuse rules remain relevant.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 45,000,000 is the principal aggregate related-party transaction threshold commonly relevant to the exemption from full related-party documentation for taxpayers below the threshold, subject to transaction-specific exceptions and statutory documentation rules. A Local File may nevertheless be required for particular categories or transactions, including certain high-risk transactions. A Master File is generally relevant where the taxpayer belongs to a qualifying multinational or domestic group. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate regime branded as Economic Substance Regulations comparable to certain offshore jurisdictions. Nevertheless, Spanish anti-abuse principles require genuine commercial rationale, real functions, appropriate personnel, assets, decision-making, risk assumption, and documentary evidence. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule, the conflict-in-application rule, beneficial-ownership principles, controlled foreign company rules, hybrid-mismatch rules, interest limitation rules, and principal-purpose analysis may deny benefits or recharacterize arrangements lacking substance. A Spanish SL manufacturing model-kit products should align its personnel, production assets, inventory, quality control, procurement, sales, and risk profile with its declared remuneration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and concealed income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining undisclosed sales channels, understating export or online-platform revenue, using false invoices, diverting customer payments to foreign accounts, or deliberately claiming fictitious expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties may range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to assessment of tax, late-payment interest, and surcharges. Tax fraud may become a criminal offense where the amount of tax defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 for the relevant tax, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded; aggravated cases carry higher penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil liability, subsidiary liability for tax debts where statutory conditions are met, disqualification consequences, and criminal liability. Courts may order restitution, asset seizure, and, in criminal cases, imprisonment. Travel restrictions are not automatic but may be imposed by judicial order where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Value added tax fraud and carousel arrangements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for non-existent supplies, misreporting intra-EU acquisitions, manipulating import VAT, or using missing-trader structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessments, recovery of improperly claimed input VAT, interest, and administrative penalties commonly calculated as a percentage of the unpaid or improperly credited VAT. Serious or organized fraud may trigger criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and persons who knowingly participate may incur civil and criminal liability. Company protection does not shield individuals who direct, authorize, or materially facilitate fraudulent VAT conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive royalties, management fees, interest, procurement charges, or purchase prices to foreign affiliates without demonstrable benefit, functions, risks, or arm's-length support.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may adjust taxable income, deny deductions, impose transfer-pricing documentation penalties, assess late-payment interest, and apply penalties linked to the tax shortfall. Failure to provide required documentation can attract fixed penalties or percentage-based penalties subject to statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face derivative civil liability and, where deliberate falsification or tax fraud is established, criminal exposure. A formal group policy does not cure unsupported pricing or sham services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial ownership, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Spanish SL as a conduit with no genuine activity, passing dividends or royalties through to an undisclosed beneficial owner, or claiming treaty relief through circular arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Treaty benefits and domestic exemptions may be denied; withholding tax, interest, penalties, and anti-abuse adjustments may be assessed. Sham or fraudulent structures may generate criminal tax or commercial-law liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur tax, civil, and potentially criminal liability where they knowingly implement a sham structure. Courts may disregard artificial arrangements and order restitution or asset measures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful profit extraction and disguised distributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Making undocumented shareholder loans, paying personal expenses through the company, declaring dividends without distributable profits, or using related-party transactions to bypass withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The amounts may be recharacterized as dividends, salary, or non-deductible expenses, generating corporate tax, personal income tax, withholding tax, social-security exposure, interest, and penalties. Unlawful distributions may also create corporate restitution claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable under Spanish company law for unlawful distributions, creditor damage, breach of fiduciary duties, and failure to preserve corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, sanctions, and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash, structuring payments, dealing with sanctioned counterparties, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, or failing to identify customers and suppliers in high-risk transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML breaches may result in significant administrative fines, public censure, temporary restrictions, and management disqualification. Sanctions violations may trigger separate administrative or criminal consequences, including asset blocking and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face personal administrative or criminal liability where they knowingly participate in or negligently permit prohibited conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs, import, product-safety, and intellectual-property violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misdeclaring customs value or tariff classification, importing counterfeit anime or branded components, evading product-safety obligations, or selling kits without required traceability and conformity information.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include customs reassessment, seizure, destruction of goods, import restrictions, administrative fines, civil damages, and criminal prosecution for serious counterfeiting or fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil compensation, injunctions, disqualification, and criminal liability where they knowingly authorize counterfeit imports, customs fraud, or unsafe product distribution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining parallel books, fabricating inventory, omitting liabilities, falsifying board or shareholder resolutions, or failing to prepare, approve, file, or preserve annual accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible consequences include accounting sanctions, tax reassessment, commercial-registry consequences, creditor claims, director disqualification, and criminal penalties for materially false accounting or insolvency-related misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for creditor losses, wrongful trading, late insolvency filing, breach of accounting duties, and criminal falsification.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlawful permanent establishment or labor and social-security avoidance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a foreign company to operate Spanish manufacturing, warehousing, sales, or agency functions while denying Spanish taxable presence, or misclassifying employees as contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spain may assess corporate income tax, VAT, payroll withholding, social-security contributions, interest, and penalties. Labor violations may produce additional fines, back-pay obligations, and operational restrictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability for unpaid tax and social-security debts, labor claims, and criminal exposure where deliberate fraud, exploitation, or document falsification is established.
